lessons.title: Number System and Basic Arithmetic
lessons.description: Learn number types, divisibility, factors, multiples, HCF and LCM.
lessons.content:
Quantitative aptitude begins with understanding numbers and arithmetic operations.

Natural numbers: 1, 2, 3, ...
Whole numbers: 0, 1, 2, ...
Integers: Negative numbers, zero and positive numbers.
Prime numbers: Numbers greater than 1 with exactly two positive factors.
Composite numbers: Numbers greater than 1 having more than two positive factors.

BODMAS defines the usual order of arithmetic operations: Brackets, Orders, Division and Multiplication from left to right, Addition and Subtraction from left to right.

Factors divide a number exactly. Multiples are obtained by multiplying a number by integers.

HCF is the highest common factor. LCM is the least common multiple.

Example: Find HCF and LCM of 12 and 18.
Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.
Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18.
HCF = 6.
LCM = 36.

For two positive integers a and b:
HCF(a,b) × LCM(a,b) = a × b.

Divisibility rules: A number is divisible by 2 if its last digit is even, by 3 if its digit sum is divisible by 3, by 5 if its last digit is 0 or 5, and by 9 if its digit sum is divisible by 9.

Placement tip: Practice mental arithmetic, multiplication tables, squares and common fractions to improve calculation speed.

lessons.title: Percentages and Percentage Change
lessons.description: Understand percentage calculations, increases, decreases and successive changes.
lessons.content:
A percentage represents a quantity out of 100.

Percentage = (Part / Whole) × 100.

Example: A student scores 72 marks out of 90.
Percentage = (72 / 90) × 100 = 80%.

To find x% of a number N:
Value = (x / 100) × N.

Example: 15% of 800 = 120.

Percentage increase = ((New Value - Original Value) / Original Value) × 100.

Percentage decrease = ((Original Value - New Value) / Original Value) × 100.

Example: Salary increases from ₹20,000 to ₹25,000.
Increase = ₹5,000.
Percentage increase = (5000 / 20000) × 100 = 25%.

Successive percentage changes are multiplicative, not simply additive.

Example: A price increases by 20% and then decreases by 10%.
Starting price = ₹100.
After increase = ₹120.
After decrease = ₹108.
Overall increase = 8%.

Shortcut: Net percentage change for successive changes a% and b% is a + b + ab/100, using negative values for decreases.

Common conversions: 1/2 = 50%, 1/4 = 25%, 1/5 = 20%, 1/8 = 12.5%.

Placement tip: Always identify the original value used as the percentage base.

lessons.title: Ratios, Proportions and Averages
lessons.description: Solve ratio distribution, direct proportion, inverse proportion and average problems.
lessons.content:
A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind.

Example: The ratio of boys to girls is 3:2. If there are 30 boys, the number of girls is 20.

If A:B = 3:2 and the total is 100, then A = 3/5 × 100 = 60 and B = 2/5 × 100 = 40.

A proportion states that two ratios are equal.

If a/b = c/d, then ad = bc, provided denominators are nonzero.

Direct proportion: Two quantities increase or decrease in the same ratio.
Example: If 5 notebooks cost ₹100, 8 notebooks cost ₹160 at the same unit price.

Inverse proportion: One quantity increases while the other decreases proportionally.
Example: If 4 equally efficient workers complete a job in 12 days, 8 workers complete it in 6 days, assuming identical work rates.

Arithmetic average = Sum of observations / Number of observations.

Example: Average of 10, 20, 30 and 40 = 100/4 = 25.

Weighted average = Sum(value × weight) / Sum(weights).

Example: A student scores 80 in a test weighted 40% and 90 in a test weighted 60%.
Weighted average = 80 × 0.4 + 90 × 0.6 = 86.

Placement tip: For ratio problems, express quantities as multiples of a common variable before solving.

lessons.title: Profit, Loss and Discounts
lessons.description: Learn cost price, selling price, profit percentage, loss percentage and discounts.
lessons.content:
Profit and loss problems involve the cost price (CP) and selling price (SP) of an item.

Profit = SP - CP when SP > CP.
Loss = CP - SP when CP > SP.

Profit percentage = (Profit / CP) × 100.
Loss percentage = (Loss / CP) × 100.

Example: A shopkeeper buys an item for ₹800 and sells it for ₹1,000.
Profit = ₹200.
Profit percentage = (200 / 800) × 100 = 25%.

Example: An item purchased for ₹1,200 is sold for ₹1,080.
Loss = ₹120.
Loss percentage = 10%.

Marked Price (MP) is the listed price before discounts.
Discount = MP - SP.
Discount percentage = (Discount / MP) × 100.

Example: A shirt marked ₹2,000 receives a 15% discount.
Discount = ₹300.
Selling price = ₹1,700.

Successive discounts are multiplicative.
Example: Discounts of 10% and 20% on ₹1,000 produce a final price of 1000 × 0.9 × 0.8 = ₹720, equivalent to a 28% discount.

For a target profit of p%:
SP = CP × (1 + p/100).

For a target loss of l%:
SP = CP × (1 - l/100).

Placement tip: Profit and loss percentages are normally calculated using cost price, while discount percentages use marked price.

lessons.title: Simple Interest, Compound Interest and Placement Problem Solving
lessons.description: Understand interest formulas and apply efficient strategies to aptitude questions.
lessons.content:
Simple Interest (SI) is calculated on the original principal.

SI = (P × R × T) / 100.

P = Principal amount.
R = Annual interest rate in percent.
T = Time in years.

Example: Find simple interest on ₹10,000 at 8% per annum for 2 years.
SI = (10000 × 8 × 2) / 100 = ₹1,600.
Total amount = ₹11,600.

Compound Interest (CI) is calculated on the principal and accumulated interest.

For annual compounding:
A = P × (1 + R/100)^T.
CI = A - P.

Example: ₹10,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually.
A = 10000 × 1.1 × 1.1 = ₹12,100.
CI = ₹2,100.

For half-yearly compounding at a nominal annual rate, use R/2 per half-year and 2T periods, assuming the stated rate is compounded half-yearly.

Aptitude problem-solving strategy:
1. Read the question carefully.
2. Identify the given values.
3. Determine the unknown quantity.
4. Select the appropriate formula.
5. Calculate systematically.
6. Verify the answer and units.

Common placement topics include percentages, ratios, averages, profit and loss, interest, time and work, and speed and distance.

Practice under timed conditions, but prioritize correct reasoning before improving speed.

quizzes.explanation: 12 is the largest positive integer dividing both 24 and 36.
